subject: Proposal: 36-month staircase co-term + auto-renew opt-out (Aurora Analytics)
messages:
From: Tom Benson <tom.benson@aurora-analytics.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal options and co-terming question

Hi Vanessa,

Our current contract with Redwood is up for renewal in October, and we are looking at a renewal structure that aligns with our fiscal planning. Two asks from procurement and finance: 1) we'd like to co-term any new capacity with our existing enterprise agreement (October 2028 expiry) and 2) explore a 3-year "staircase" ramp (low initial commit, increasing annually).

Key constraints: Aurora needs the ability to opt-out of auto-renewal (legal prefers a 60-day notice window), and invoicing needs to remain monthly (we can't move to annual prepay for all tiers).

Can you share pricing examples for a 36-month ramp with co-terming and a version that includes a modest up-front credit? Also let us know if co-terming + auto-renew opt-out is feasible from Redwood's side and any implications on pricing or SLAs.

Thanks,
Tom
Tom Benson
Head of Procurement
Aurora Analytics

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Tom Benson <tom.benson@aurora-analytics.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Jul 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal options and co-terming question

Tom — thanks for the clear asks. High level: we can do a co-terming approach + a 36-month stair-step ramp with a monthly invoice cadence. Auto-renew opt-out is doable with an explicit 60-day notice, but there are typical guardrails we should align on (minimum notice, true-up behavior, and how credits amortize).

Attached is a working schedule (Renewal_Harmonization_3yr_v1.xlsx) showing two priced scenarios:
- Scenario A: Standard stair-step (Year1 40% commit, Year2 70%, Year3 100%) with monthly billing and a small implementation credit applied across months.
- Scenario B: Front-loaded credit (bigger upfront credit, slightly lower unit prices) but requires a 12-month partial-commit hold if they cancel before year 2.

Immediate next steps I propose:
1) I can walk procurement through Scenario A vs B in a 30-min call this week.
2) If legal insists on a 60-day opt-out, we should confirm the termination handling for reserved capacity and whether Aurora wants an automatic fallback to hosted (metered) instead of pro-rated true-up.

Looping in my pricing and renewals partners on the internal side for quick confirmation (see CC).

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Attachments: Renewal_Harmonization_3yr_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet - proposed ramp/pricing)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 13 Jul 2028 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: FW: Renewal options and co-terming question — pricing confirmation needed

Team — forwarding Aurora's ask and my initial proposal (attached). Quick asks:
- Confirm whether Scenario A (stair-step 40/70/100) needs an escalator or fixed unit price across years. Pricing should assume dedicated capacity starting in Y2.
- Is the 60-day auto-renew opt-out workable without requiring a minimum 12-month prepay? If not, what is the least-disruptive commercial compromise we can offer (partial prepay, short partial-commit)?
- Any SLA or capacity guarantees we must flag (burst windows, guaranteed slot reservations) that would affect legal/finance?

Deal details: DEAL-3419-AUR — Aurora already consumes significant hosted capacity; this is for expansion + reserved pool. Region: US.

Can you reply with redlines/suggested language and an updated schedule by EOD Friday so I can get back to their procurement person?

Thanks,
Vanessa

From: Tom Benson <tom.benson@aurora-analytics.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@aurora-analytics.com
Date: Mon, 17 Jul 2028 14:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: 36-month staircase co-term + auto-renew opt-out (Aurora Analytics)

Vanessa — we reviewed the spreadsheet with finance and legal. A few points from our side:
- Procurement prefers Scenario A (the lighter front-load), but they need a clear statement that monthly invoices will remain a firm requirement.
- Legal is firm on the 60-day opt-out; they will not accept a clause that converts unpaid months into a lump-sum prepay upon termination. Instead they want a pro-rata true-up based on consumed capacity only.
- We also asked for an explicit early-termination cap: if Aurora cancels within the first 12 months, liability capped at 20% of remaining committed value.

I've attached a draft SOW with those notes inserted (Signed_SOW_Draft.pdf) — it's not signed, it's a redline for discussion. Can your team incorporate the early-termination cap and confirm the monthly invoice commitment and pro-rata true-up language?

Thanks,
Tom
Head of Procurement
Aurora Analytics
Attachments: Signed_SOW_Draft.pdf (redline - SOW with termination language)

Date: Fri, 20 Jul 2028 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: 36-month staircase co-term + auto-renew opt-out (Aurora Analytics) — next steps

Tom — appreciate the clear feedback and the SOW redline. We can meet all three asks with a small set of commercial guardrails that I'll summarize below and capture in an updated schedule (attached Renewal_Harmonization_3yr_v2.xlsx):

1) Monthly invoicing: confirmed. Aurora will be billed monthly for committed capacity; any metered overage will show as separate line items.
2) Auto-renew opt-out: 60-day notice confirmed. To balance risk we propose a 30-day notice for downgrades of reserved capacity (so we retain scheduling predictability), but we will accept Aurora's 60-day opt-out for full termination.
3) Early-termination cap: we can accept a 20% cap on remaining committed value if termination occurs within the first 12 months. After 12 months, standard pro-rata true-up on consumed capacity applies.
4) Credits amortization: implementation credit in Scenario A will amortize monthly over the first 12 months; if Aurora terminates within 12 months, remaining unamortized credit will reduce any final true-up liability.

Next steps I propose:
- I'll upload the updated SOW and schedule to DocuSign this afternoon (link below) for Aurora legal to review.
- Karthik/Priyom/Marissa: please confirm the language above is acceptable and if so I will push the DocuSign envelope. If you need alternative wording for the downgrade vs termination notice windows, flag it by EOD Monday.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/transaction/ABC-aurora-renewal
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/DEAL-3419-AUR
